text:
alex: heads-up, i'm chasing a couple of weird edge cases in the new rl-based orchestration. saw two tenant-level bursts that bypassed admission and took down a worker pool for ~30s.

maria: ugh, details? which bypass path — cache hit, fallback, or mis-routed shard?

alex: seems like a combination. quota-proxy returned a soft-allow on `fast-path` during failover, then admission-service lost connectivity -> fallback to local token bucket. local buckets were generously sized for bursts so a tenant could blow through while global controller was partitioned.

sam: so basically split-brain between global controller and local proxies. did we have circuit-breaker on fallback path?

alex: not really — fallback was intentionally permissive to avoid 5xx during brief controller hickups. tradeoff backfired at scale.

jen: is there a way to tighten fallback without increasing errors? maybe a graded fallback: allow X tokens/sec for N seconds then drop to conservative mode.

tao: +1 to graded fallback. also we should propagate a transient backpressure signal from proxies to the router, so upstream can shed non-critical routes.

maria: agree. proposal: on controller disconnect, proxies enter `degraded-mode` with a conservative token quota and emit `bp=soft` tag to LB. LB uses that to avoid routing heavy batch requests to degraded proxies.

sam: how would we compute the conservative quota? static % of nominal or adaptive based on recent usage?

alex: adaptive is better but tricky. we can keep a short sliding window (30s) and set fallback quota = min(peak*0.2, baseline) to avoid zeroing out small tenants. also cap by absolute tokens to protect infra.

jen: want to call out fairness: when degraded-mode hits, we should prioritize small interactive requests over large background batches. so admission rules must accept `priority` hints from route metadata.

ta0: typo on my name above :) tao.

tao: on prioritized admission — we need to avoid trusting clients entirely. add server-side mapping: route -> priority, with a per-tenant override policy that ops can change.

maria: ops change needs rollout safety. small admin tweak should not instantly re-prioritize a noisy tenant. add a probation window and telemetry alert.

sam: also consider lease rebalance frequency. current plan rebalances every 60s which may be too slow during short partitions. but lowering freq increases churn. any middle ground?

alex: thought: add an event-driven rebalance on signals (node-liveness, sustained queue growth) and keep periodic as fallback. event-driven rebalance would be rate-limited (e.g., at most once per 10s) to avoid thrash.

jen: what about metrics? we need metrics that correlate to perceived customer pain: `p99_tail_latency`, `admission_reject_rate`, `fallback_mode_duration`, `tokens_consumed_fallback`. add tenant-scoped versions.

rls-bot: deploy-check: admission-service (v2.3.1) has no fallback-cap config; quota-proxy (canary) has `fallback_mode` feature-flag. runbook link: https://redwood/sops/rls-fallback-runbook

alex: actionable next steps i propose: 1) add conservative fallback caps + graded decay (sam to sketch), 2) emit backpressure tag from proxies to router (tao to prototype), 3) event-driven rebalance + rate-limit (maria to prototype), 4) add tenant-scoped fallback metrics and alert (jen to own).

maria: ack, i'll add a short RFC note for event-driven rebalance with sample flow diagrams.

sam: i'll draft the fallback-cap sketch, including formula and config knobs. will post a tiny config example: 
```
fallback_mode: degraded
max_tokens_per_min: 1200  # conservative cap
burst_window_sec: 15
decay_factor: 0.6
```

jen: i'll add the metrics dashboard panels and an alert recipe. wondering if we should wire an automated canary: when fallback_mode_duration > 10s for >3 nodes, auto-escalate to oncall.

ta0: tao again :) but yes, automated canary makes sense. can we also have a tenant-probation list so we can temporarily throttle a repeat offender with minimal ops?

alex: add probation list to the runbook as a manual step, and we can automate later once we have reliable signals.

maria: ok team — i'll sync with security about potential abuse-case playbooks. let's check back in 48h with sketches. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all. i'll open the tracking issue and link the sketches.
